# Five Robot XApp SDK

Independent native firmware (.bin / ESP-IDF): read docs/native-firmware-ai.md first.
It contains both board profiles, wiring and native delivery rules. Download only that document initially; do not run the XApp workflow for a native firmware task. XApp native-ui templates remain XApps.

SDK 2026.10.29.2; API 2.16; package format 1. Preserve API<=2.15 imports and layouts.
New BLE session/beacon, UDP/WS, UTC and native8k playback need matched API2.16 firmware.
Release-ready artifacts are separate from public availability: follow the official index and docs/releases.md. AMBE is experimental/default OFF; DMR0.1.1 is a connection-test app without voice calls; published history stays immutable. See docs/api-2.16.md for capability and experimental limits.

Official index: https://site.flashbot5.com/developer/v1/index.json
GitHub: https://github.com/Yoriuml/five-robot-app-docs
Gitee: https://gitee.com/yorium/five-robot-app-docs

Mandatory XApp AI execution entry: docs/ai-workflow.md
Use workflow.py prepare/build. Read only the returned capability context and target template first.
Full stable rules remain in docs/ai-reference.md; do not load all of them for every APP.
One source-filled JSON request can use workflow.py run. Tool-owned model calls: zero.
See docs/workflow-automation.md. Do not repeat manual checks already covered by build.
Implementation scope and evidence boundaries: docs/ai-rules-rollout.md
Shared tool and optional asset dependency cache: docs/environment-cache.md
Default templates have cached licensed launcher assets; no third-party Python packages are needed.
tools/check_product.py checks final package presentation; build enables it by default.
Do not treat static, host, final-WASM preview or hardware results as interchangeable.

Pin one immutable release; reuse verified local SDK/toolchain files.
Use actual API contracts, final package checks and separate static/stub/runtime/hardware evidence.
Product input roles differ from historical CONFIRM/BACK ABI names; follow the documented target profile.
No invented SDK declarations, implicit firmware/API edits, credential disclosure or automatic device operations.
User needs and authorization govern task scope.
